bibl.title: Subliminal messages exert long-term effects on decision-making

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Whether novel relational information presented below awareness is stored well enough to bias a conscious decision made twenty minutes later.
span.quote: We speculated that subliminal messages might affect delayed decision-making especially if messages contain several pieces of novel information that must be relationally bound in long-term memory.

span.label: existence
span.quote: This is unprecedented evidence of the longevity and impact of subliminal messages on conscious, rational decision-making.

span.label: long-term subliminal influence on delayed decision-making
span.quote: We asked if humans can rapidly integrate and store novel relational information (e.g. “person X is a manager”, see Fig. 1a ) from subliminal messages for later use in a decision-making situation (e.g. “guess the income of X”).

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: We ran two experiments to test whether subliminal stimulus pairs would affect delayed decision-making ( Figure 1a ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: Relational encoding of multiple stimuli engages hippocampus ( Henke et al., 1997 ; Duss et al. , 2014 ), which learns rapidly and stores relations for long term due to its exceptional plasticity ( McClelland et al. , 1995 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: It is known that the processing of single items engages neocortex ( Henke et al., 1997 ; Duss et al. , 2014 ), which forms long-term memory traces rather slowly over many learning trials ( McClelland et al. , 1995 ).

span.label: The proposed route is relational binding in the hippocampal system, which can encode novel relations rapidly and hold them durably
span.quote: Relational binding engages the hippocampal memory system, which can rapidly encode and durably store novel relations.

span.label: That predicts the opposite of the usual expectation - subliminal effects should last longer when the material is novel and must be bound, not when it is familiar and repeated
span.quote: These studies suggest that subliminal messages are only slowly stored and might not be stored at all if they provide novel, unfamiliar information.

span.label: In the second experiment the same logic is applied to word meaning: a subliminal German word must be decoded and linked to a foreign word for the later judgement to work
span.quote: Hence, the meaning of subliminal German words was decoded, linked to foreign words, and stored to influence lexical–semantic decisions 20 min following subliminal encoding.

span.label: Awareness is ruled out four ways rather than one: interview, two objective tests, Bayes factors, and a regression on residual awareness
span.quote: We further performed a multiple regression analysis to assess whether potential awareness of faces or occupations predicted decision accuracy in the main experiment, and to estimate whether accuracy remained above chance level if the theoretical awareness in both tests is 0 (i.e., whether the intercept is significant).

span.label: A stricter check: removing every participant whose awareness score deviated from chance in either direction, and confirming the effect survives
span.quote: In a final step, we excluded those participants from the analysis of the data from the main experiment, who tended to perform above or below chance level in either of the two awareness tests (12 participants exhibited an awareness score with a binomial probability of P < 20%).

span.label: The paradigm cannot establish what kind of memory was formed - precise semantic relations or only fuzzy semantic/affective associations.
span.quote: The long-lasting influence of subliminal stimulus pairs evinces nonconscious relational learning, but the experimental paradigms employed in this study do not pin down the exact nature of the unconsciously formed memories.

span.label: In experiment 2 the Bayes analysis of the awareness test was inconclusive, so true unawareness of the subliminal words was not established.
span.quote: Whether participants were truly unaware of the subliminal words thus remains elusive.

span.label: The awareness test for experiment 2 may simply have been insensitive rather than showing absence of awareness.
span.quote: The resulting factor for the awareness test (mean accuracy = 1.3% above chance level, SE = 1.16%) was 1.14, which suggests that the test was not sensitive enough to reject stimulus awareness.

span.label: Awareness was not probed trial-by-trial during the main experiments, so brief awareness of some stimuli cannot be excluded.
span.quote: Because we did not assess awareness of each subliminal stimulus immediately following the respective encoding episode in the main experiments, we cannot rule out the possibility that participants were briefly aware of some of the subliminal images.

span.label: The authors state plainly that a non-significant awareness test does not establish unawareness, and this is why they compute Bayes factors
span.quote: However, the nonsignificant tests do not reveal whether participants were truly unaware (i.e. whether H0 can be accepted), or whether our tests were not sensitive enough to detect awareness.

span.label: In Experiment 2 that check came back inconclusive and is reported as such - awareness could not be excluded
span.quote: The resulting factor for the awareness test (mean accuracy = 1.3% above chance level, SE = 1.16%) was 1.14, which suggests that the test was not sensitive enough to reject stimulus awareness.

span.label: The conclusion for Experiment 2 is therefore explicitly left open on the awareness question
span.quote: Whether participants were truly unaware of the subliminal words thus remains elusive.

span.label: The regression method used to separate awareness from effect is cited together with the criticism of it
span.quote: Although subject to criticism (e.g. Miller, 2000 ), this method is used widely to assess whether subliminal influences on behavior are independent of stimulus awareness.

span.label: The effects are a few percentage points above chance in both experiments
span.quote: Mean decision accuracy was 53.97% (95% CI [51.25, 56.96]), which exceeded the chance level of 50% ( t (45) = 2.94, P = 0.005; r = 0.40) ( Fig. 1b ).

span.label: The Experiment 2 effect rests on a p just under .05
span.quote: On average, 52.7% (95% CI [50.1, 55.2]) ( Fig. 1b ) of synonyms were classified accurately, which exceeded chance level (two-tailed t -test: t (33) = 2.128; P = 0.041; r = 0.35).

span.label: a non-significant awareness test - as ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE: the test may simply have been too insensitive, which proves nothing
span.quote: However, the nonsignificant tests do not reveal whether participants were truly unaware (i.e. whether H0 can be accepted), or whether our tests were not sensitive enough to detect awareness.

span.label: a non-significant awareness test - as EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE: a Bayes factor below one third, which is what Experiment 1 obtained
span.quote: Both factors were below 1/3, indicating substantial evidence for the null hypothesis, i.e. that participants were not aware of the masked stimuli.

span.label: the same test in Experiment 2 - INCONCLUSIVE: a factor near one, favouring neither hypothesis, and reported rather than glossed
span.quote: The resulting factor for the awareness test (mean accuracy = 1.3% above chance level, SE = 1.16%) was 1.14, which suggests that the test was not sensitive enough to reject stimulus awareness.

span.label: subliminal effect - the received view: decays within about a second, which is why it is thought harmless
span.quote: Subliminal manipulation is often considered harmless because its effects typically decay within a second.

span.label: subliminal effect - as found here: undiminished at 25 minutes compared with 15, for novel relational material
span.quote: Mean decision accuracy was not significantly smaller after 25 compared to 15 min (53.04% vs. 54.90%; two-tailed t (44) = 0.68, P = 0.50; r = 0.10), which indicates that the effect of subliminal encoding persisted through both retention intervals at equal strength.

span.label: builds-on → Duss et al. (2011) subliminal masking paradigm
span.quote: We used a well-established paradigm to render stimuli invisible ( Duss et al. , 2011 ).

span.label: builds-on → Greenwald et al. (1995) regression method for estimating awareness-independent subliminal effects
span.quote: This method was brought forward by Greenwald et al. (1995) .

span.label: contradicts → prevailing views that consciousness is a precondition for information integration, relational learning and decision-making (Tononi, 2004; Shanks, 2010; Newell and Shanks, 2014)
span.quote: The finding that subliminally processed information is rapidly integrated and stored to guide delayed decisions challenges prevailing views of the cognitive function of consciousness.

span.label: critiques → the view that subliminal effects decay within a second and are therefore harmless
span.quote: Subliminal manipulation is often considered harmless because its effects typically decay within a second.

span.label: critiques → the assumption that subliminal messages are stored only slowly and not at all when novel
span.quote: These studies suggest that subliminal messages are only slowly stored and might not be stored at all if they provide novel, unfamiliar information.

span.label: extends → Dienes on using Bayes factors to test whether a null can be accepted
span.quote: We, therefore, calculated Bayes factors for the two t -tests following the recommendations provided in Dienes (2008 , 2014 ).

span.label: extends → Greenwald et al.'s regression method for separating subliminal influence from residual awareness
span.quote: This method was brought forward by Greenwald et al. (1995) .

span.label: relational binding —operationalised-as→ hippocampal memory system
span.quote: Relational binding engages the hippocampal memory system, which can rapidly encode and durably store novel relations.

span.label: subliminal —causes→ long-term memory
span.quote: Hence, new semantic associations were stored for long term affecting the direction of decision-making almost half an hour later.

span.label: masked —operationalised-as→ subliminal
span.quote: An interview that was administered after the main experiment to assess subjective awareness of the masked stimuli suggested that none of the participants had seen the subliminal faces or words during encoding.

span.label: Bayes factors —operationalised-as→ awareness test
span.quote: We, therefore, calculated Bayes factors for the two t -tests following the recommendations provided in Dienes (2008 , 2014 ).

span.label: prior distribution —part-of→ Bayes factors
span.quote: Assuming that awareness of subliminal stimuli should yield recognition accuracy that is comparable to performance in the decision task (3.97% above chance level), we chose a half-normal prior distribution with a mode of 0 and a standard deviation of 3.97% to calculate BF ( Dienes, 2014 ).

span.label: decision accuracy —contrasted-with→ chance level
span.quote: Mean decision accuracy was 53.97% (95% CI [51.25, 56.96]), which exceeded the chance level of 50% ( t (45) = 2.94, P = 0.005; r = 0.40) ( Fig. 1b ).

span.label: awareness test —distinct-from→ decision accuracy
span.quote: Neither potential awareness of faces ( β = 0.16, t (41) = 0.88, P = 0.383) nor potential awareness of occupations ( β = 0.24, t (41) = 1.2, P = 0.23) predicted decision accuracy in the main experiment.

span.label: face–occupation pairs —operationalised-as→ relational binding
span.quote: In experiment 1, subliminal face–occupation pairs affected conscious decisions about the income of these individuals almost half an hour later.

span.label: lexical–semantic decisions —operationalised-as→ long-term memory
span.quote: In experiment 2, subliminal presentation of vocabulary of a foreign language enabled participants to later decide whether these foreign words are presented with correct or incorrect translations.

span.label: retention intervals —contrasted-with→ subliminal
span.quote: Subliminal influence did not significantly decay if probed after 25 versus 15 min.

span.label: unconscious processing —same-as→ subliminal
span.quote: We, therefore, conclude that there was no awareness of encoding stimuli in the main experiment and that long-term effects derived from unconscious processing alone.

span.quote: We found that participants, who were unaware of the presence and purpose of subliminal information, successfully processed subliminal face–word and nonword–word pairs and formed lasting unconscious semantic relational memories based on only one or two subliminal encoding episodes (each comprising 12 adjacent subliminal stimulus repetitions).
